sourceEvidence: The first-pass lamp pole was two independently generated concrete cylinders meeting at Y=2.10 m: lower diameter 0.190 m and upper diameter 0.150 m. That creates an abrupt 20 mm radial step rather than the continuous manufactured taper expected of a purpose-made lighting pole.

The old GroundMoistureBand used a 0.196 m diameter around a 0.190 m base pole, making weathering a 3 mm radial geometry bulge on every side. The requested causal-weathering rule requires the moisture/splash state to change optical/material response without inventing a raised dirt sleeve.

The old head relied on generic Neck/Cap/DiffuserCrown cylinders around the topology-aware PhysicalDiffuser, but did not lock real insertion/retention relationships between the pole top, adapter, diffuser necks and weather cap.

The first-pass lamp had no modeled service-access interface. A benchmark-visible public lighting pole therefore lacked a manufactured access/maintenance cue and risked reading as a generic procedural post.

The first draft of the new custom tapered-pole mesh used intuitive a-b-c side winding. Static vector cross-product audit showed those triangles faced inward; bottom/top cap winding was also reversed. The substantive final code corrects side normals and both caps before any Unity render is claimed.

referenceResearch.use: construction-class reference only: lighting poles may use a continuous taper from larger base diameter to smaller top diameter; the cited page describes steel road-lighting poles and is not treated as exact historical dimensional evidence for this fictional concrete park pole
supports treating pole-top diameter/insertion and luminaire attachment as a real interface rather than a decorative floating head; no exact product compatibility is claimed
current municipal-park morphology reference showing a simple pole plus retained globe form in an ordinary neighborhood park; not used as proof of a 2000 product model

qaEnforcement: Contract validation requires manufacture, dimensions/thickness, component interfaces, geometry-vs-material allocation, material optical values, cause-based aging, LOD policy, critical-fail rules and explicit zero Visual Fidelity credit.
Scene QA rejects the old stacked-pole/moisture/head renderers if still visible or if any remain bound into formal LOD renderer arrays.
PhysicalPole QA requires a two-submesh custom taper, 0.04-0.12 m below-grade embed, top Y within 4 mm, at least 3.98 m physical height, and grade/top radii within 2 mm of contract values.

Curved service-interface QA measures shell radial ranges from real generated mesh vertices at top/bottom and rejects positive cover/gasket gaps above 3 mm, penetration above 8 mm, or drift from the designed 0.5 mm bearing overlap.

Head-interface QA derives real mesh Y envelopes and rejects pole/adapter, adapter/lower-retainer, lower-retainer/diffuser, diffuser/upper-retainer and upper-retainer/cap gaps or penetrations outside hard limits.

Final scene QA requires dielectric concrete/paint/diffuser/EPDM, metallic exposed fasteners after the microdetail pass, no daytime emissive diffuser, no generated colliders and no active stock Cube/Cylinder/Sphere/Capsule mesh in the lamp.

Formal park-furniture LOD validation now calls the completed park-lamp QA after shared microdetail, so the existing Native 4K review packet inherits the lamp checks before/after evidence stages without creating a parallel scoring path.
No source-side pass clears a rendered critical defect and no Visual Fidelity point is awarded by this QA.
